source.title: Relevance of Rotationally Equivariant Convolutions for Predicting Molecular Properties
source.authors: Benjamin Kurt Miller; M. Geiger; T. Smidt; Frank No'e

record.file_problem: The full paper and supplementary material are present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: It reports a controlled architecture ablation with test error outcomes, but its molecular equivariance comparison does not test the listed image-convolution versus fully connected version.
record.gate_note: The authors compare rotationally invariant and equivariant networks on QM9 test data. This is evidence about architectural choices and test error, but none of the listed versions specifically covers rotational equivariance for molecular-property regression. SchNet, SchNetPack and Cormorant results in Table 1 are comparator figures, not this study's own runs.
record.test_reason: The study tests rotational equivariance versus invariant internal features for molecular regression on QM9. None of V1–V8 covers this comparison. In particular, V3 concerns convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers; both principal architectures here use molecular convolutions. Using Adam and searching batch sizes does not constitute an optimizer or batch-size comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors report a 23% average MAE reduction from rotationally equivariant internal features at fixed depth and parameter count, versus 4% from an additional invariant convolutional block. They recommend equivariant internal layers for tensor-magnitude regression when angular contributions matter, while acknowledging difficulty identifying which targets generally benefit most.
record.recipe_differences: A QM9 molecular-property architecture ablation comparing rotationally invariant with rotationally equivariant convolutions; it does not test the listed generalization versions directly.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by target: the authors say the equivariance ablation had the most impact on dipole moment, electronic spatial extent and U0; L0Net Deep worsened predictions on Cv and µ.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed depth and parameter count, L1Net has lower test MAE than L0Net on all 12 QM9 targets, averaging a 23% reduction relative to L0Net. Adding an invariant convolutional block gives a 4% average reduction, with worse MAE on dipole moment and heat capacity and unchanged rounded MAE on polarizability. L0Net Deep slightly outperforms L1Net on HOMO.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the tested QM9 molecular-regression architecture, introducing rotationally equivariant internal features improves test MAE more on average than adding an invariant convolutional block.

record.problems: The study reports test MAE but not training error or a generalization gap. Its ablation is limited to QM9 molecular regression and does not address random-label memorization, image architectures, or the listed optimizer, batch-size and regularization versions. Reported uncertainty intervals are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: None of the authors' own Table 1 L1Net, L0Net and L0Net Deep target results were omitted. Comparator results for SchNet, SchNetPack and Cormorant were left out because they are not this study's own runs.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classification, local connectivity, learned sparsity, and convolution-based initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning and recovery recipes.
Controlled batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects, training-set-size dependence, underfitting, and removal with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All 36 own-model Table 1 values and subjects match the text. The states indicate lack of applicability to V1–V8, not unreadable MAEs. Section 4.3 reports choosing the architecture using test-set performance across 40 hyperparameter configurations, which qualifies interpretation of the reported test results. Supplementary depth variants report validation curves but do not test any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Image classification; convolution versus fully connected networks; local connectivity; learned sparse connections or convolution-based initialization.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptation of training recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
